grammar.title: The Passive: Present and Past Simple
grammar.explanation:
We use the **passive** when the action matters more than the person who does it. We also use it when we do not know who did it.

Form it with **be + past participle**. Use **is/are** for the present and **was/were** for the past.

Only **be** changes. The past participle stays the same, for example **made**, **built**, or **written**.

Use the **passive** for news, science, and processes. **Acid rain is caused** by pollution, and **air pollution is measured** in cities every day.

Use **by** only when the person matters. **The atmosphere is studied by** scientists, but never add **by people** or **by someone**.

Questions and negatives use **be**, not **do**. Ask **Was the bridge built** in 1932, not **Did the bridge built**.
examples: *Coffee **is grown** in Brazil and Colombia.* (present: a general fact)
*The Harry Potter books **were written by** J. K. Rowling.* (by + the writer)
*Millions of emails **are sent** every day.* (present: plural)

practice.q: Rewrite in the passive: People measure air pollution in cities every day.
practice.a: Air pollution is measured in cities every day.

practice.q: Rewrite in the passive: Acid rain damaged the trees last summer.
practice.a: The trees were damaged by acid rain last summer.

practice.q: Rewrite in the passive: Scientists study the atmosphere every day.
practice.a: The atmosphere is studied every day.

practice.q: Rewrite in the passive, about your brother: A dog bit my brother.
practice.a: My brother was bitten by a dog.
